comparisons.peer_topic: Credit Rating Agency Assignments for Subsidiaries and Obligations
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit rating agencies assign ratings to the senior unsecured debt obligations of Group Inc., as well as long- and short-term issuer ratings and deposit ratings for specific subsidiaries including GS&Co., GSI, GS Bank USA, GSIB, and GSBE, along with ratings for certain other subsidiaries.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs disclose details regarding credit ratings and their associated obligations. Citigroup quantifies the potential increase in cash and collateral obligations resulting from a potential downgrade. In contrast, Goldman Sachs' disclosure focuses on the administrative aspect of credit rating agencies assigning specific issuer and debt obligations to the group and its subsidiaries (such as GS&Co., GSI, and GS Bank USA), without providing a comparable quantitative estimate of the liquidity impact of a potential downgrade.

sentences.text: In total, as of December 31, 2024, Citi estimates that a one-notch downgrade of Citigroup Inc. and Citibank across all three major rating agencies could result in increased aggregate cash obligations and collateral requirements of approximately $0.2 billion, compared to $0.2 billion as of September 30, 2024.
The credit rating agencies assign credit ratings to the obligations of Group Inc., which directly issues or guarantees substantially all of our senior unsecured debt obligations.
GS Bank USA, GSIB and GSBE have also been assigned long- and short-term issuer ratings, as well as ratings on their long- and short-term bank deposits.

comparisons.peer_topic: Uncertainty of Credit Rating Downgrade Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: The impact of a credit rating downgrade on business and results of operations is inherently uncertain and depends on factors such as the magnitude of the downgrade, peer ratings, and client behavior.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley disclose the uncertainty and potential liquidity impacts of credit rating downgrades. However, Citigroup provides a specific quantitative estimate ($0.2 billion increase in cash/collateral obligations for a one-notch downgrade), whereas Morgan Stanley explicitly states that the impact is 'inherently uncertain' and depends on factors like client behavior, without providing a comparable specific dollar-amount estimate in this disclosure. Both confirm that liquidity impacts from collateral requirements are included in their stress tests.

sentences.text: In total, as of December 31, 2024, Citi estimates that a one-notch downgrade of Citigroup Inc. and Citibank across all three major rating agencies could result in increased aggregate cash obligations and collateral requirements of approximately $0.2 billion, compared to $0.2 billion as of September 30, 2024.

While certain aspects of a credit rating downgrade are quantifiable pursuant to contractual provisions, the impact it would have on our business and results of operations in future periods is inherently uncertain and would depend on a number of interrelated factors, including, among other things, the magnitude of the downgrade, the rating relative to peers, the rating assigned by the relevant agency before the downgrade, individual client behavior and future mitigating actions we might take.
The liquidity impact of additional collateral requirements is included in our Liquidity Stress Tests.
